title: hooks.map.json
description: Which audit runs when a file changes, for hooks/audit_on_edit.py. Lives at .design-suite/hooks.map.json in the project being audited, because what is worth auditing on save is a property of the project, not of the suite. The runner is advisory-only: nothing declared here can block a tool call or write a file.

name.description: What the user sees when this entry has something to say.

glob.description: fnmatch pattern(s) against the repo-relative path of the changed file. Fires on Write/Edit/NotebookEdit only.

commandPattern.description: Regex against a Bash tool call's command. Fires on Bash only. This is the shape pr_reminders.py uses to catch `git commit` / `gh pr create`.

command.description: Argv to run, from the project root. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is expanded. IMPORTANT: an audit run at narrowed scope must not write to the artefact its whole-repo run owns. audit_tokens.py defaults --out to .design-suite/tokens-findings.json; a hook that scopes it to one directory and lets it write there replaces a full sweep with a partial one, and /design-debt then grades the project on a fraction of it. Redirect --out (and never pass --findings) in a scoped entry.

scopeMode.description: What scopeArg passes: the changed file, or its containing directory. Every audit in bin/ takes --dir and cannot audit a single file, so "dir" is what those entries need.

scopeArg.description: How the changed path is passed to the command — a flag like "--file" (flag then path), or true to append the path bare. REQUIRED unless wholeRepo is set: an unscoped audit on every save re-runs CI's work on a keystroke loop, which is the mistake this field exists to make visible.

wholeRepo.description: Declare that this entry deliberately audits the whole project on every trigger. Only correct when the audit is genuinely cheap or the artefact is one combined document — mock_api_reminders.py regenerates openapi.json this way, and says why in its docstring. Set `reason` alongside it.

reason.description: Why wholeRepo is justified for this entry. Read by humans, not the runner.

reportWhen.description: What counts as something worth saying. "nonzero" suits a gate that fails on a violation (the copy gate). "findings" suits a report that always exits 0 (audit_tokens exits 0 on 144 findings and on none) — the runner reads findingsPath instead and reports the count. Pointing an entry at a report with "nonzero" makes it permanently silent, which reads as a clean codebase.

findingsPath.description: Where this entry's command wrote its findings envelope (its --findings path). Required when reportWhen is "findings". Use a scratch path, never the whole-repo findings file.

fixHint.description: Command to suggest when this entry reports something, e.g. "/sync-mock-api <contract>".

reportClean.description: Say so even when the audit passes. Off by default — a confirmation on every save trains people to stop reading these.

repair.description: An optional repair command for this entry's findings, run by bin/run_precommit_audits.py at commit time. It is handed ONLY the changed files that this commit touched, and only ever for the on-change bucket: whole-repo band-1 repair was measured at 0 of 33 findings fixed on an already-migrated codebase (RFC-0003 §3a), because on cold code the deterministic cases are already migrated and the survivors are band 2 and band 3 by construction. The command must emit a unified diff on stdout and write nothing (RFC-0003 §3c) — the runner prints the diff and never applies it, stages it, or commits it. A repair offer never removes a finding from the report: a finding with no available fix is listed with the reason there is none, because an unfixed finding that prints like a fixed one is the failure this suite is built against.

command.description: Argv to run, from the project root. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is expanded.

filesArg.description: Flag the changed file paths are appended after, e.g. "--files". REQUIRED: without it the runner would have to run the repairer repo-wide, which is both the 0-of-33 shape and an offer to rewrite code this commit never touched. Declared without it, the runner refuses and says no fix was offered.

bandsArg.description: Optional flag for a path the command writes {file, line, kind, band} records to (bin/repair_tokens.py's --bands-json). Without it the runner cannot attribute an offer to a specific finding and says so per finding rather than guessing.

disabled.description: Keep the entry, stop running it.

preCommit.description: Eligible to run in bin/run_precommit_audits.py, the pre-commit hook this suite can install (see bin/install_precommit_hook.py). Distinct from being wired into audit_on_edit.py (which every entry is, regardless of this flag): the on-save runner is advisory-only and never blocks, while a pre-commit run gates the commit — reportWhen decides pass/fail the same way it decides what audit_on_edit.py reports ('nonzero' fails on a bad exit code, 'findings' fails on a non-empty findingsPath). Only set this on an entry that is genuinely fast (seconds, not minutes — this runs on every commit, not every push) and invariant (a real regression, not a judgment call a human still has to make). Most entries in this file should NOT set it: a slow or fuzzy audit that gates every commit trains people to reach for --no-verify, which is worse than not gating at all. Note that the pre-commit runner scopes findings to the lines the commit actually changed (RFC-0003 §3a), which only works for an entry whose reportWhen is "findings" — a "nonzero" entry emits no {file, line} records to filter, so it is run and reported whole and labelled as unscoped rather than being reported clean.
